body: The human body can be described at several scales. Molecules form cellular structures; cells cooperate within tissues; tissues form organs; and organs work together in systems. These levels describe relationships within a single living organism.

The heart, blood and blood vessels form a transport system. The respiratory system exchanges gases with the surroundings, while muscles and skeletal structures enable movement. Other systems coordinate responses, process nutrients and maintain internal conditions. Their functions overlap: no organ system is completely independent of the rest of the body.

limitations: The model describes general human biology; individuals differ in anatomy, development and function.
purpose: Introduce cells, tissues, organs and systems as nested levels of organization.
